did_you_know.text: Did you know? Achish king of Gath asked David to join him and his soldiers in the campaign against Israel, and David gave him an answer that was not entirely explicit.
Did you know? The chapter mentions two things related to Saul’s policies: Samuel had already died and been buried at Ramah, and Saul had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land.
Did you know? The Philistines camped at Shunem, while the Israelite army under Saul’s leadership camped at Gilboa—two places mentioned as the staging points for the battle.
Did you know? Saul inquired of the LORD, but received no answer by any of the means mentioned: through dreams, the Urim, or the prophets.
Did you know? Although Saul had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land, when he was in distress he asked his servants to find him a medium at Endor.
Did you know? Saul disguised himself, put on different clothes, and went to the medium at night with two men so that his identity would not be revealed.
Did you know? Saul swore to the medium by the LORD that she would not be punished for what she was about to do—even though the chapter had already described his opposition to mediums.
Did you know? The medium described the figure as “an old man” coming up, wearing a robe, and from this description Saul understood that it was Samuel.
Did you know? Samuel told Saul that on the next day Saul, his sons, and the army of Israel would be handed over to the Philistines, repeating the severe judgment he had announced to him.
Did you know? After Saul collapsed and had no strength left, the medium quickly prepared a fattened calf and unleavened bread; after they ate, Saul and his servants left that night for the camp.
